results.name: Afghanistan
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the people counting Afghanistan's flood dead do not work for Afghanistan. The United Nations reported on 22 July 2026 that at least 26 people were killed, 23 of them in Nuristan province, after flash floods struck eastern Afghanistan on 20 and 21 July 2026.

results.name: India
results.key_finding: Why it matters: India’s government gave the students what they asked for, but only after the police had beaten them. Human Rights Watch reported on 23 July 2026 that on 20 July, security forces used tear gas and batons against a peaceful march on Parliament and shut down mobile internet in central Delhi.

results.name: Delhi
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the crackdown that drew two international human rights organisations happened on Delhi’s streets, carried out by Delhi Police. Human Rights Watch reported on 23 July 2026 that on 20 July, security forces used tear gas and batons and shut down mobile internet in central Delhi.

results.name: Mumbai
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Mumbai appeared in this cycle because people marched there, not because Mumbai did anything to them. Bloomberg reported on 23 July 2026 that solidarity demonstrations tied to the national exam-leak movement spread to Mumbai alongside Bengaluru, Kolkata, Patna and Ahmedabad.

results.name: Kolkata
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Kolkata was flagged for hosting protests, not for suppressing them. Bloomberg reported on 23 July 2026 that solidarity demonstrations tied to the national exam-leak movement were held in Kolkata alongside Mumbai, Bengaluru and Patna.

results.name: Lahore
results.key_finding: Why it matters: nearly all of the deaths that put Pakistan in the news were not in Lahore. The Washington Times reported on 27 July 2026 that 109 people had died nationwide since 26 June 2026, with nearly half in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, several hundred kilometres from Lahore.

results.name: Detroit
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the harm here was federal, and Detroit’s officials objected to it. About a week before 15 July 2026, three Detroit officials wrote to the Department of Homeland Security urging an end to dangerous vehicle pursuits in residential neighbourhoods.

results.name: Atlanta
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the Atlanta flag is about what residents did, not what the city did. Nearly 100 people held a candlelight vigil outside the downtown federal immigration field office on Saturday 25 July 2026, calling for due process for detained immigrants.

results.name: Guatemala City
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the conduct that flagged Guatemala City was not the city’s. Inter Press Service reported on 24 July 2026 on Guatemala’s captured national justice system, describing a state long in the hands of what Guatemalans call the pact of the corrupt.

results.name: UnitedHealth Group
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the number that matters is older than the headline. The federal finding that UnitedHealthcare denied 71% of long-term acute-care hospital admission requests was published by the HHS Office of Inspector General on 8 June 2026, not in July.

results.name: Palantir AI
results.key_finding: Why it matters: a court had already said this data could not be used for immigration enforcement, and it was used for immigration enforcement anyway. Court filings made public on 17 July 2026 show Immigration and Customs Enforcement forwarded improperly obtained Medicaid data to Palantir.

results.name: Sudan
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Sudan is not recovering from famine, it is sliding back toward it. The World Food Programme warned on 14 July 2026 that conflict, aid-funding cuts and shipping disruption threaten to reverse the gains made after famine took hold.

results.name: Charter Communications
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Charter did not just lose a discrimination case, it was penalised for trying to make the complaint go away. A New York appeals court upheld on 23 July 2026 a finding that Charter Communications unlawfully retaliated against employee Jon E. Eisen after he filed an age-discrimination complaint.

results.name: University of California, San Diego
results.key_finding: Why it matters: this is a federal accusation, not a court ruling, and the university denies it. The Department of Justice Civil Rights Division announced on 20 July 2026 that UC San Diego’s School of Medicine unlawfully used race in admissions in violation of Title VI.

results.name: GEO Group
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the July news about GEO Group is about what a bank did, not what GEO Group did. Citizens Bank announced on 17 July 2026 that it had ended its lending relationships with GEO Group and CoreCivic.

notes: BACKFILL RUN. Assessor stage for the 2026-07-27 night, the final night of a four-night catch-up, reconstructed on 2026-07-28. assessment_date is 2026-07-27 in every artifact. No digest, no briefings, no index writes, no proposal applications, no git commit. DATE DISCIPLINE. No evidence dated after 2026-07-27 was scored, cited or referenced. Every score-moving source was fetched or searched and its publication date verified against the source itself. Background sources older than the 2026-07-13 to 2026-07-27 window are used only for standing structural context and are labelled with their true dates. CLAIMS DROPPED ON DATE VERIFICATION. Four. (1) UNITEDHEALTH GROUP: the scan presented the HHS Office of Inspector General finding that UnitedHealthcare denied 71 per cent of long-term acute-care hospital admission requests as a July item with evidence_date 2026-07-17. The OIG report is dated 8 June 2026, verified against the OIG report page and Beckers Payer Issues coverage. This is the article-date-as-event-date pattern. Re-dated to its true date and treated as pre-window background; the in-window item scored is the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations records demand from Senators Blumenthal and Hawley, mid-July 2026. (2) GEO GROUP: the scan cited a Cal/OSHA workplace-safety settlement as in-window. Direct fetch of the CalMatters article shows it is dated 7 July 2026, before the window opened, and that the settlement itself was signed in May 2026. Dropped as in-window evidence, recorded as labelled background. (3) ATLANTA: the scan attributed the abandonment of a roughly one billion dollar ICE detention warehouse expansion to the July window. DHS ended the plan in June 2026, reported 18 June 2026 by Georgia Public Broadcasting and 19 June 2026 by CNN. It also concerns Social Circle, Georgia, a separate municipality of about 5,000 people, not the City of Atlanta. Dropped on both date and attribution grounds. (4) AFGHANISTAN: the scan reported roughly 80 injured and over 100 missing. Neither figure could be tied to an in-window dated statement. The United Nations report of 22 July 2026 records at least 26 killed and nine injured. The uncorroborated figures were not scored. DATE CORRECTIONS APPLIED WITHOUT DROPPING THE ITEM. Two. (a) GEO GROUP: the Citizens Bank lending exit was dated 2026-07-20 by the scan from an undated PhillyVoice article; the announcement is dated 17 July 2026 per U.S. News and GBH. Re-dated, still in window. (b) ATLANTA: the vigil was dated 2026-07-26 by the scan; the Atlanta News First article is dated 25 July 2026 and gives the event as Saturday 25 July 2026. Re-dated, still in window. GATE WARNINGS RESOLVED, MIXED DATED AND UNDATED SOURCING, all four handled. UNITEDHEALTH GROUP: both scan sources are dated and were verified; the undated element was not needed. GEO GROUP: the undated PhillyVoice source was not used at all; dated U.S. News and Fortune reports were used instead. LAHORE: the Daily Pakistan and Pakistan Today reports were located through dated search results and are cited at claim level without verbatim quotes; the score-moving dated source is The Washington Times of 27 July 2026. UC SAN DIEGO: both sources are dated; the Department of Justice release returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch, so its content is carried through KPBS of 21 July 2026, which quotes the Assistant Attorney General directly. GATE WARNINGS RESOLVED, URL DATE LATER THAN EVIDENCE DATE, all four confirmed as follow-up coverage rather than staleness. INDIA: triggering events are 18 July 2026, the forced hospitalisation of Sonam Wangchuk, and 20 July 2026, the tear gas, batons, and internet and metro shutdown; Human Rights Watch of 23 July 2026 is follow-up. UNITEDHEALTH GROUP: triggering event is the mid-July Senate letter; Minnesota Reformer of 22 July 2026 is follow-up, and the 71 per cent figure it repeats belongs to the 8 June 2026 OIG report. DELHI: triggering event is 20 July 2026; both Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International are follow-up. UC SAN DIEGO: triggering event is the DOJ announcement of 20 July 2026; KPBS of 21 July 2026 is follow-up. All scored against the triggering event date. ATTRIBUTION RULE APPLIED to eight entities. AFGHANISTAN: flash floods are a natural hazard, not state conduct; only detection, warning, response and repair capacity were scored. SUDAN: donor funding cuts are the conduct of donor states, not Sudan. MUMBAI and KOLKATA: the documented excessive force occurred in Delhi and was carried out by Delhi Police; both cities hosted peaceful assembly only. LAHORE: the nationwide monsoon toll of 109 since 26 June 2026, nearly half in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is not attributed to Lahore; only Lahore-specific drainage failure was scored. GUATEMALA CITY: judicial persecution is national conduct by the Public Ministry and the courts, not the municipality. DETROIT and ATLANTA: federal immigration enforcement conduct is not city conduct. GEO GROUP: a lender exit decision and a federal appeals ruling in CoreCivic favour are not GEO Group conduct. FLOOR ENTITIES. Afghanistan, Sudan and Palantir AI are all published at composite 0, the lowest score on their indexes. A floor entity cannot move lower. All three confirm at 0 with delta 0 and sustained watch flags. PRE-ADJUDICATION SCREENS APPLIED. Two. UNITEDHEALTH GROUP: a congressional records demand is an investigation, not a court finding, and the denial-of-care pattern is already priced into the baseline set on 29 May 2026 and confirmed on 6 July 2026. UC SAN DIEGO: the Department of Justice Title VI finding of 20 July 2026 is a contested agency determination in an open enforcement matter with no court decision, and the university publicly disputes it. Both recorded as watch flags rather than scored as established conduct. ANTI-FALSE-POSITIVE SCREENS APPLIED. Five. GEO GROUP is the material one: the assessed composite of 11.9 sits 5.3 points above the published 6.6, which numerically crosses the proposal threshold, but the entire gap is an arithmetic artifact. GEO Group publishes all eight dimensions at 1.5, which reconstructs canonically to 12.5, not 6.6. No upgrade proposal was emitted; the discrepancy is filed as a math-hygiene referral. INDIA carries a positive delta of 1.3 driven by verified in-window government concessions, the education minister resigning on 25 July 2026 and all three protester demands being accepted, but the entity surfaced on negative evidence, so no upgrade proposal was emitted and the movement remains sub-threshold. DETROIT: the city officials letter to DHS predates the window at about 8 July 2026 and was recorded as labelled background rather than scored as in-window positive conduct. ATLANTA and ABRIDGE carry positive deltas of 0.3 each, inside normal assessment variance, and neither is backed by new positive in-window conduct. ASSESSOR-VARIANCE CONTROL. DELHI was anchored to research/assessments/delhi-2026-07-21.md at composite 31.9 and moved only on the five dimensions with direct in-window evidence, rather than re-deriving all 40 subdimensions from scratch. This produced a delta of -4.7, below the proposal threshold, where an unanchored re-derivation produced roughly -6.5. The anchored figure was used because the difference between the two is assessor-to-assessor variance, not new conduct. BAND CROSSINGS. None. No entity assessed this cycle crossed a band, and band_change is false on all 20 results. The two-source, one-tier-4-minimum bar for band crossings was therefore not engaged. MATH-HYGIENE RECONSTRUCTION. Canonical reconstruction was run against the published dimensions of all 20 entities. Nineteen reconstruct within the 0.5-point tolerance. One does not: GEO GROUP, published composite 6.6 against a canonical 12.5, difference 5.9. This is independently confirmed by node site/scripts/validate-indexes.mjs, which emits it as a warning at two places in fortune-500.json. It is referred for maintenance and was not re-litigated. Vanuatu, the known open issue, was not in this cycle and was not touched. ROTATION-STATE. last_assessed and last_evidence_touch set to 2026-07-27 for exactly the 20 entities actually assessed. No composite, band or rank value was changed to a proposed figure, and last_change_proposal was not touched on any entity because zero proposals were generated. Two rank drifts were found among the 20 and corrected to the published index values, both instances of the known 324-entity one-rank drift referred for separate reconciliation: India rank 154 corrected to 155, Charter Communications rank 318 corrected to 317. No other entity was stamped. UNASSESSABLE. None. All 20 entities were assessed. gilead-sciences was excluded from the list on instruction and was not assessed. OUTCOME. 20 assessed, 20 confirmations, 0 change proposals, 0 band changes. Ten entities carry watch flags.
